\begin{tablenotes}
\small
\item \textit{Notes:} $^{+}p<0.10$, $^{*}p<0.05$, $^{**}p<0.01$,
$^{***}p<0.001$. Panel A reports HC1 standard errors in parentheses for
the two conventional columns. For DT-IIV it reports BOTH valid standard
errors: the pairs bootstrap in parentheses and the corrected three-step
analytic standard error of Corollary~\ref{cor:var_est} in brackets. The
naive standard error that treats $\widehat{\mathbf S}$ as data is not
reported here; see Table~\ref{tab:app_inference}. Stars on the DT-IIV
column come from the bca bootstrap interval.
\item The DT instrument is $\mathbf s=\mathbf x+k\delta\mathbf r$ with
$\mathbf r\perp\mathbf x$ by construction, so
$\mathrm{cor}(\mathbf S,\mathbf x)=\{1+\delta^2 B/A\}^{-1/2}$ is a
deterministic decreasing function of $\delta$: it restates $\delta$ rather
than testing it. The relevance floor in Panel B is therefore an
assumption about how weak an instrument is acceptable, and
Table~\ref{tab:mroz_sensitivity} maps that assumption to the estimate.
\item Where $\widehat M(\delta)$ has more than one root, $\delta_0$ is
not pinned down by the moment alone and the identification-robust
interval is the summary to read.
\item First-stage and overidentification statistics treat the instrument
as data. They are reported for the traditional IV column only and are
uninformative for a generated instrument
(Remark~\ref{rem:ols_identity}).
\item The DT sign is selected once on the estimation sample and imposed on
every bootstrap resample, so the bootstrap and the analytic covariance
condition on $\mathbf k$ identically.
\item The bootstrap interval and the standard-error based test
disagree about zero on this sample. The interval respects the skewness
of the bootstrap distribution; the standard-error test imposes
normality. Both are reported.
\end{tablenotes}
